claims.text: Toughness retention in high-entropy alloys is governed by heterogeneous local lattice strain.
Heterogeneous lattice strain causes unusual dislocation behaviors, including multiple kinks or jogs and bidirectional cross-slip.
Heterogeneous lattice strain induces nanometer-scale twinning.
Complex dislocation structures and nanoscale twins cooperatively shield crack tips through crack deflection and bridging.
The proposed crack-tip shielding delays crack propagation and failure.
Nano-twinning is an important additional deformation mode that contributes to retaining toughness in CrCoNi between room and cryogenic temperatures.
The proposed initial CrCoNi or similar alloy has measurable heterogeneous lattice strain.
The proposed initial alloy exhibits nano-twinning during plastic deformation.
A minor alloying addition or optimized annealing treatment can reduce local lattice-strain heterogeneity.
Homogenizing the local chemical environment homogenizes the local strain environment.
Dislocation slip and nano-twinning can both contribute to deformation from room temperature to cryogenic temperatures in the proposed alloy class.
The density and distribution of kinked dislocation cores and nanoscale twin boundaries are the structural mediators of toughness.
Alloys with greater lattice-strain heterogeneity will have greater fracture toughness than the untreated baseline.
Reducing lattice-strain heterogeneity will suppress kinked or otherwise complex dislocation behavior.
Reducing lattice-strain heterogeneity will decrease nano-twin density.
Reducing lattice-strain heterogeneity will decrease fracture toughness relative to the untreated condition.
The hypothesis is limited to single-phase or near-single-phase, especially FCC, high- or medium-entropy alloys in regimes where dislocation motion and twinning both contribute to plasticity.
The hypothesis may not apply to heavily phase-separated alloys or deformation dominated by diffusion-controlled creep.
Failure to observe statistically significant decreases in both nano-twin density and fracture toughness after verified strain homogenization would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome compares a high-strain-heterogeneity alloy against an untreated baseline, but the baseline is itself defined as having inherent heterogeneous lattice strain, so the purported high-versus-baseline contrast is not clearly distinct.

The experiment specifies identical nominal compositions while also allowing a minor alloying adjustment as the homogenizing intervention; an alloying adjustment would make the nominal compositions different.
